children: BRT.Fit, a fitness app that combines smart wearable devices, real-world exercise, and on-chain incentives, has rolled out a series of product updates. According to ChainCatcher, the app updated its user guide on July 7 to simplify downloading, Web3 mode access, wallet connection, and test reward claims, and it launched on the Apple App Store on July 9 under the name BitRing.

On July 29, the app received a major interface redesign and began requiring a connected smart device before users could participate in fitness tasks. On August 12, a new version added an AI fitness interface, onboarding for new users, and Oura Ring integration, followed by automatic language adaptation on August 14 and a simplified onboarding flow for Web2 users on August 29.

The app is also available on Google Play as a health and fitness app. On August 27, BRT.Fit upgraded its smart contract, temporarily suspending reward claims and staking functions during the process. As of September 13, the community said participation had exceeded 10,000 users, the iOS version had been submitted for App Store review, and the team was preparing to expand into Southeast Asia.

title: BRT.Fit Updates Fitness App With AI Interface, Oura Ring Integration, and App Store Review Submission
